callouts: **Hamstring recurrence is real but moderate.** A prior hamstring injury makes the next injury **1.44× more likely** to be another hamstring.
**Knee injuries are especially sticky.** Prior knee injuries raise same-region recurrence to **1.50× baseline**.
**Head/neck shows the strongest recurrence.** Prior concussion or head/neck injury raises same-region risk to **1.93× baseline**.
**The risk stays local.** Prior knee injuries do not meaningfully increase future hamstring or ankle/foot injuries.
**One healthy year does not reset the risk.** Same-region recurrence is about **15%** the next season and **15%** two seasons later.
injuryPredictability.calloutSummary: Overall, the next injury occurs in the same body region **15% of the time — 1.21× above baseline**. Injury history is most useful when it is **body-part specific**, not as a blanket “injury-prone” label.

callouts: **Age has little effect on injury odds.** Players ≤24 were injured 52% of the time vs 51% for players 31+, though older players missed slightly more time once hurt.
**Prior workload adds little signal.** Heavy-workload players were injured **55%** of the time vs **51%** for light workloads (p ≈ 0.10).
**Prior injury raises future risk only modestly.** Players with a prior injury were hurt **53% vs 49%**, with little difference in severity.
